title.de: Machen lassen: I had my hair cut
title.sl: Dati narediti: I had my hair cut
title.it: Farsi fare: I had my hair cut

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj daš narediti drugemu (I had my hair cut, I'm getting the van fixed), in to ločiš od tega, kar narediš sam, ter od I had cut my hair.
goal.de: Du sagst, was du machen lässt (I had my hair cut, I'm getting the van fixed), und unterscheidest es von dem, was du selbst machst, und von I had cut my hair.
goal.it: Dici che cosa ti fai fare (I had my hair cut, I'm getting the van fixed) e lo distingui da quello che fai da solo e da I had cut my hair.
goal.en: You can say what you have done for you (I had my hair cut, I'm getting the van fixed), and keep it apart from what you do yourself and from I had cut my hair.

say.sl: **have** + stvar + deležnik pomeni, da to zate naredi nekdo drug: **I had my hair cut.** ({m:Dal|f:Dala} sem si postriči lase.) **Mrs Birkett had the roof mended.** (Gospa Birkett je dala popraviti streho.) Če narediš {m:sam|f:sama}, je to navaden glagol: **I cut my hair.**
say.de: **have** + Sache + Partizip heißt, dass jemand anderer es für dich macht: **I had my hair cut.** (Ich habe mir die Haare schneiden lassen.) **Mrs Birkett had the roof mended.** (Mrs Birkett hat das Dach reparieren lassen.) Machst du es selbst, ist es ein normales Verb: **I cut my hair.**
say.it: **have** + cosa + participio vuol dire che lo fa un altro per te: **I had my hair cut.** (Mi sono fatt{m:o|f:a} tagliare i capelli.) **Mrs Birkett had the roof mended.** (Mrs Birkett ha fatto riparare il tetto.) Se lo fai da sol{m:o|f:a}, è un verbo normale: **I cut my hair.**
say.en: **have** + thing + the participle means someone else does it for you: **I had my hair cut.** **Mrs Birkett had the roof mended.** If you do it yourself, it's a plain verb: **I cut my hair.**

say.sl: Spremeni se le **have**: **We're having the roof mended.** (Streho nam prav zdaj popravljajo.) **We've had the roof mended.** **We'll have the roof mended.** Vprašanje in zanikanje kot pri vsakem glagolu: **Did you have your hair cut?** (Si se {m:dal|f:dala} postriči?) **I didn't have it done.**
say.de: Nur **have** ändert sich: **We're having the roof mended.** (Wir lassen gerade das Dach reparieren.) **We've had the roof mended.** **We'll have the roof mended.** Frage und Verneinung wie bei jedem Verb: **Did you have your hair cut?** (Hast du dir die Haare schneiden lassen?) **I didn't have it done.**
say.it: Cambia solo **have**: **We're having the roof mended.** (Stiamo facendo riparare il tetto.) **We've had the roof mended.** **We'll have the roof mended.** Domanda e negazione come per ogni verbo: **Did you have your hair cut?** (Ti sei fatt{m:o|f:a} tagliare i capelli?) **I didn't have it done.**
say.en: Only **have** changes: **We're having the roof mended.** **We've had the roof mended.** **We'll have the roof mended.** Questions and no as with any verb: **Did you have your hair cut?** **I didn't have it done.**

say.sl: V govoru je pogosto **get**, enak pomen: **I got my hair cut.** **I'm getting the van fixed.** (Kombi mi prav zdaj popravljajo.) Tudi kot ukaz: **Get your hair cut!** (Pojdi se ostrič!) Američani rečejo tudi **I've gotten my hair cut.**, Britanci **I've had my hair cut.**
say.de: Gesprochen ist **get** häufig, mit demselben Sinn: **I got my hair cut.** **I'm getting the van fixed.** (Ich lasse gerade den Lieferwagen reparieren.) Auch als Befehl: **Get your hair cut!** (Lass dir die Haare schneiden!) In Amerika auch **I've gotten my hair cut.**, in Großbritannien **I've had my hair cut.**
say.it: A voce è comune **get**, con lo stesso senso: **I got my hair cut.** **I'm getting the van fixed.** (Sto facendo riparare il furgone.) Anche come ordine: **Get your hair cut!** (Fatti tagliare i capelli!) In America anche **I've gotten my hair cut.**, in Gran Bretagna **I've had my hair cut.**
say.en: In talk **get** is common, with the same meaning: **I got my hair cut.** **I'm getting the van fixed.** As an order too: **Get your hair cut!** Americans also say **I've gotten my hair cut.**, the British **I've had my hair cut.**

say.sl: Pazi na vrstni red: **I had my hair cut.** (nekdo drug) ni **I had cut my hair.** ({m:ostrigel|f:ostrigla} sem se {m:sam|f:sama}, še prej). Stvar stoji v sredini, za njo deležnik: **I had the gate mended** (nikoli *I had the gate mend*). Pri **cut** sta osnovna oblika in deležnik enaka, pri drugih ne: **painted, cleaned, looked at**.
say.de: Achte auf die Reihenfolge: **I had my hair cut.** (jemand anderer) ist nicht **I had cut my hair.** (selbst, schon vorher). Die Sache steht in der Mitte, danach das Partizip: **I had the gate mended** (nie *I had the gate mend*). *lassen* ist hier nicht *let*. Bei **cut** sind Grundform und Partizip gleich, sonst nicht: **painted, cleaned, looked at**.
say.it: Attent{m:o|f:a} all'ordine: **I had my hair cut.** (un altro) non è **I had cut my hair.** (da sol{m:o|f:a}, già prima). La cosa sta in mezzo, poi il participio: **I had the gate mended** (mai *I had the gate mend*). Qui *fare* non è *make*. Con **cut** forma base e participio sono uguali, con gli altri no: **painted, cleaned, looked at**.
say.en: Mind the order: **I had my hair cut.** (someone else) isn't **I had cut my hair.** (myself, earlier). The thing stands in the middle, then the participle: **I had the gate mended** (never *I had the gate mend*). With **cut** the base form and the participle look the same, with others they don't: **painted, cleaned, looked at**.

say.sl: Kdo je to naredil, pove **by**: **We had the gate mended by Mr Dixon.** Če je oseba v ospredju: **get** + oseba + **to**: **I'll get Jack to look at it.** ({m:Prosil|f:Prosila} bom Jacka, naj to pogleda.) Ali **have** + oseba + osnovna oblika: **I'll have Jack look at it.** Slednje je v Britaniji bolj uradno.
say.de: Wer es gemacht hat, sagt **by**: **We had the gate mended by Mr Dixon.** Steht die Person im Vordergrund: **get** + Person + **to**: **I'll get Jack to look at it.** (Ich lasse Jack einen Blick darauf werfen.) Oder **have** + Person + Grundform: **I'll have Jack look at it.** Das klingt in Großbritannien förmlicher.
say.it: Chi l'ha fatto lo dice **by**: **We had the gate mended by Mr Dixon.** Se conta la persona: **get** + persona + **to**: **I'll get Jack to look at it.** (Lo faccio vedere a Jack.) Oppure **have** + persona + forma base: **I'll have Jack look at it.** In Gran Bretagna suona più formale.
say.en: **by** says who did it: **We had the gate mended by Mr Dixon.** When the person matters: **get** + person + **to**: **I'll get Jack to look at it.** Or **have** + person + the base form: **I'll have Jack look at it.** In Britain that sounds more formal.

say.sl: Ista oblika pove tudi kaj slabega, česar nisi {m:hotel|f:hotela}: **Old Wilf had his wallet stolen on the bus.** (Staremu Wilfu so na avtobusu ukradli denarnico.) **Sam had his van broken into.** Ni naročil, zgodilo se mu je. To je isto kot **His wallet was stolen.**
say.de: Dieselbe Form sagt auch etwas Schlimmes, das du nicht wolltest: **Old Wilf had his wallet stolen on the bus.** (Dem alten Wilf wurde im Bus die Geldbörse gestohlen.) **Sam had his van broken into.** Bestellt hat er das nicht, es ist ihm passiert. Das ist dasselbe wie **His wallet was stolen.**
say.it: La stessa forma dice anche qualcosa di brutto che non volevi: **Old Wilf had his wallet stolen on the bus.** (Al vecchio Wilf hanno rubato il portafoglio sull'autobus.) **Sam had his van broken into.** Non l'ha chiesto lui, gli è successo. È come **His wallet was stolen.**
say.en: The same form says something bad you didn't want: **Old Wilf had his wallet stolen on the bus.** **Sam had his van broken into.** He didn't ask for it; it happened to him. It's the same as **His wallet was stolen.**

translation.sl: Gospa Birkett ima veliko dela. Prejšnji mesec je dala popraviti streho, ta teden ji pleskajo kuhinjo. Naslednji teden bo dala očistiti okna. Včeraj je gospoda Dixona pripravila do tega, da je popravil vrata. Harry se mora ostriči. Ni se strigel od junija.
translation.de: Mrs Birkett hat viel zu tun. Letzten Monat hat sie das Dach reparieren lassen, diese Woche lässt sie die Küche streichen. Nächste Woche lässt sie die Fenster putzen. Gestern hat sie Mr Dixon dazu gebracht, das Tor zu reparieren. Harry muss zum Friseur. Seit Juni war er nicht mehr dort.
translation.it: Mrs Birkett ha molto da fare. Il mese scorso ha fatto riparare il tetto, questa settimana fa dipingere la cucina. La settimana prossima farà pulire le finestre. Ieri ha fatto riparare il cancello a Mr Dixon. Harry deve farsi tagliare i capelli. Non se li fa tagliare da giugno.
translation.en: Mrs Birkett is busy. She had the roof mended last month, and this week she is having the kitchen painted. Next week she's going to have the windows cleaned. She got Mr Dixon to mend the gate yesterday. Harry needs to get his hair cut. He hasn't had it cut since June.
